title: What Happens When You Stand Up Too Fast?
sources: Merck Manual Professional, 'Orthostatic Hypotension' ('Normally, the gravitational stress of suddenly standing causes blood (1/2 to 1 L) to pool in the veins of the legs and trunk'; the drop in venous return lowers cardiac output and BP; baroreceptors in the aortic arch and carotid sinus activate reflexes that rapidly return BP to normal, raising heart rate; 'Symptoms of faintness, light-headedness, dizziness, confusion, or blurred vision occur within seconds to a few minutes of standing'): https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/cardiovascular-disorders/symptoms-of-cardiovascular-disorders/orthostatic-hypotension

Mayo Clinic, 'Orthostatic hypotension (postural hypotension)' (symptoms include lightheadedness or dizziness upon standing and blurry vision; when you stand, gravity causes blood to collect in the legs and belly and blood pressure drops; special cells (baroreceptors) near the heart and neck arteries sense the lower pressure and signal the brain, which tells the heart to beat faster and pump more blood): https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/orthostatic-hypotension/symptoms-causes/syc-20352548

Cleveland Clinic, 'Orthostatic Hypotension' (blurred vision is a listed symptom; diagnosed by a drop of 20 mmHg top / 10 mmHg bottom within three minutes of standing; give yourself more time to stand; call a provider if you often get dizzy when standing; immediate care for fainting, falls or chest pain): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/9385-low-blood-pressure-orthostatic-hypotension

Cleveland Clinic Health Essentials, 'Dizzy When Standing' (blood can settle or pool in the veins in your lower body; 'your blood pressure in your brain drops which causes you to feel dizzy'; sit on the edge of the bed for a couple seconds before standing; if this is happening often, see your doctor): https://health.clevelandclinic.org/dizzy-when-standing

UCLA Health, 'Feel dizzy when you stand up? What it means and what to do about it' (some people call it a 'head rush'; the medical name is orthostatic or postural hypotension): https://www.uclahealth.org/news/article/feel-dizzy-when-you-stand-up-what-it-means-and-what-do-about

NHS, 'Low blood pressure (hypotension)' (blurred vision and dizziness; symptoms when you stand up may be postural hypotension; get up slowly; see a GP if symptoms keep happening): https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/low-blood-pressure-hypotension/

Tease (next video): Cleveland Clinic, 'Ulnar Nerve' (your funny bone isn't a bone, it's a nerve; the tingle comes from pressure on the ulnar nerve at the elbow): https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/body/21664-ulnar-nerve

Up to a liter of blood moves. Toward your head, or your legs?
